_schema: Room content. The renderer's trust boundary, enforced in room.js:
_plain: PLAIN TEXT, escaped on render: cards[].name, groups[].title, groups[].symbols[].n
_raw: RAW AUTHORED HTML, injected as-is: cards[].body, cards[].note, examples[].q, examples[].steps[], examples[].ans, groups[].symbols[].g
_rule: Anything moved between those two lists changes what the browser does with it. Plain fields must never contain markup; raw fields are trusted and must never hold anything a reader typed.

cards.name: Molarity
cards.note: moles of solute per litre of solution — not per litre of solvent.

cards.name: Dilution
cards.note: Moles of solute don't change when you add water, so concentration × volume is conserved.

cards.name: Molality
cards.note: Uses mass of solvent, so it doesn't drift with temperature the way molarity does.

cards.name: Preparing a solution
cards.body: Weigh the solute, dissolve in less than the final volume, then top up to the mark.
cards.note: Never add solvent to the mark first — the solute has volume too.

cards.name: Solution stoichiometry
cards.body: moles = M × V. Get moles, use the mole ratio, convert back.
cards.note: The balanced equation still governs the ratio.

cards.name: Net ionic equation
cards.body: Split every soluble strong electrolyte into ions, then cancel whatever appears on both sides.
cards.note: What cancels are the spectator ions.

cards.name: Will it precipitate?
cards.body: Swap the partners and check each product against the solubility rules.
cards.note: No insoluble product means no reaction.

cards.name: Parts per million
cards.note: For dilute aqueous solutions, 1 ppm ≈ 1 mg/L.
